49
RAJYA  SABHA
————
List of Questions for ORAL ANSWERS
to be asked at a sitting of the Rajya Sabha to be held on
Wednesday, December 5, 2012/Agrahayana 14, 1934 (Saka)
————
(Ministries: Commerce and Industry; Culture; Defence; Home Affairs;
Housing and Urban Poverty Alleviation; Labour and Employment;
Social Justice and Empowerment; Textiles; Women and
Child Development)
Total number of questions — 20
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
Muslims in jails of the country
*161. SHRI SABIR ALI: Will the
Minister of HOME AFFAIRS be pleased
to state:
(a) the details of innocent Muslims
languishing in various jails of the country;
and
(b) the mechanism being worked out to
avoid avoidable harassment of Muslims?
People languishing in jails on
charges of extremism
†*162. SHRI RAM VILAS PASW AN:
Will the Minister of HOME AFFAIRS be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that a large
number of people are in jail on charges of
extremism;
(b) whether it is a fact that a large
number of innocent people are acquitted
honourably after spending long time in jail;
and
(c) if so, whether Government will set
up fast track courts for alleged extremists
that courts could take immediate decision?
Dismal performance in protecting
vulnerable communities
*163. SHRI PIYUSH GOYAL: Will the
Minister of HOME AFFAIRS be pleased
to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that leading
international human rights organisations
have reported India's dismal performance
in protecting vulnerable communities;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether Government has taken
steps in this regard;
(d) if so, the details thereof; and
(e) if not, the reasons therefor?
Funds allocated and spent under
ICDS
*164. SHRI VIJAY JAW AHARLAL
DARDA: Will the Minister of WOMEN
AND CHILD DEVELOPMENT be

50
pleased to state:
(a) whether awareness amongst mothers
about 'nutrition' is being created through
launching  of special campaigns in 112 focus
districts in six States—Bihar, Jharkhand,
Madhya Pradesh, Odisha, Rajasthan and
Uttar Pradesh which were covered by the
survey conducted by Citizens' Alliance
Against Malnutrition (January, 2012);
(b) whether any shortcomings have been
brought to the notice of Government in the
implementation of Integrated Child
Development Services (ICDS) Scheme as
this scheme reaches out to millions of
underprivileged children; and
(c) how much funds were allocated and
actually spent on the above scheme, during
2009-10, 2010-11 and 2011-12?
Unearthing of sites of historical
importance
†*165. SHRI JUGUL KISHORE: Will
the Minister of CULTURE be pleased to
state:
(a) whether certain sites of historical
importance were found during excavation
work in the country;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether several important historical
sites are being destroyed in the country
due to rapid increase in human habitation;
(d) if so, Government's response
thereto; and
(e) whether Government proposes to
conduct a survey to identify such sites and
if so, the details thereof?
Establishment of Real Estate
Regulatory Authority
*166. SHRI C.M. RAMESH: Will the
Minister of HOUSING AND URBAN
POVERTY ALLEVIATION be pleased to
state:
(a) whether Government proposes to
establish a Real Estate Regulatory
Authority for regulation and planned
development in the real estate sector; and
(b) if so, the details thereof?
Eradication of manual scavenging
*167. DR. JANARDHAN
WAGHMARE: Will the Minister of
SOCIAL JUSTICE AND
EMPOWERMENT be pleased to state:
(a) whether the Central Government has
recently taken up the cause of eradicating
manual scavenging, an inhuman and
outlawed practice that still exists in several
parts of the country;
(b) if so, whether the State Governments
have been given any directions and
assistance in this regard;
(c) if so, the details thereof; and
(d) by when the entire country will be
free from the menace of manual scavenging?
Shortage of houses for lower
income group
†*168. SHRI RAM JETHMALANI:
Will the Minister of HOUSING AND
URBAN POVERTY ALLEVIATION be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that there is
maximum shortage of those houses which
are within the reach of families of lower
income group in the country;
(b) if so, Government's reaction thereto;
(c) whether it is also a fact that under
Government's housing policy , maximum
houses which are being constructed at
present in the country are beyond the reach
of the most needy groups; and
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

51
(d) if so, Government's reaction thereto
and whether Government would make
changes in this housing policy?
Fresh surveys for identification of
bonded labour problems
*169. SHRI ISHWAR SINGH: Will the
Minister of LABOUR AND
EMPLOYMENT be pleased to state:
(a) whether the Supreme Court has
recently directed the Central Government
and various State Governments to conduct
fresh surveys to identify bonded labour
problems in the country;
(b) if so, whether it is a fact that a large
number of children continue to work as
domestic helps even after the enactment of
the Right to Education Act; and
(c) if so, the concrete steps the Central
Government proposes to take to identify
such children and ensure that they get
proper education?
Unemployment rate
*170. SHRIMATI GUNDU
SUDHARANI: Will the Minister of
LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT be
pleased to state:
(a) the year-wise and State-wise
unemployment rate (in per cent terms) in
the States, during the last five years;
(b) the details of unemployment
percentage in the country as per the latest
report of Labour Bureau;
(c) the factors that have contributed for
high and low percentage of unemployment
in various States during the above period;
and
(d) the efforts Ministry is making to
bring down the rate of unemployment in
the States?
Business leaders shying away from
innovation
*171. SHRI D.P. TRIPATHI: Will the
Minister of COMMERCE AND
INDUSTRY be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the Business
leaders have begun to shy away from
innovation or new projects;
(b) if so, the reasons therefor;
(c) whether it is also a fact that it leads
to discouragement in investment and
growth; and
(d) if so, the steps Government is taking
in this regard?
Low share of agricultural
commodities in world market
*172. SHRI N. BALAGANGA: Will
the Minister of COMMERCE AND
INDUSTRY be pleased to state:
(a) whether India's share of agricultural
commodities in the world market is very
low;
(b) if so, the details thereof and the
reasons therefor;
(c) the year-wise, commodity-wise and
country-wise details of total quantity of
agricultural commodities like rice, wheat,
pulses, sugar, etc. imported and exported
along with revenue generated during the last
two years and the current year;
(d) whether such export of commodities
has affected the domestic supply and
demand scenario; and
(e) if so, the details thereof, along with
the steps taken to ensure proper domestic
supply?

52
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
Urging ASEAN to expand business
prospects
*173. SHRI KUMAR DEEPAK DAS:
Will the Minister of COMMERCE AND
INDUSTRY be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that India is now
urging the Association of South East Asian
Nations (ASEAN) market to expand its
business prospects;
(b) whether it is also a fact that future
business prospects between India and
ASEAN in areas of agriculture, IT,
education, health care, mining and tourism
is also bright; and
(c) if so, Government's recent policy in
this regard, including details of various
infrastructure developments in road, air and
other communication with the time-frame
of completion of such projects included
under the policy?
Damage due to cyclone 'Nilam' in
Tamil Nadu
*174. SHRI BALWINDER SINGH
BHUNDER: Will the Minister of HOME
AFFAIRS be pleased to state:
(a) whether the cyclone 'Nilam' hit the
Tamil Nadu coast recently;
(b) if so, the details of the loss of lives
and property;
(c) the extent of relief and rehabilitation
of persons affected by the cyclone;
(d) whether warning of the cyclone was
given to people in advance; and
(e) if so, the details thereof and the
evacuation carried out to shift people to
safe place?
Communal riots in the country
*175. SHRI MOHAMMED ADEEB:
Will the Minister of HOME AFFAIRS be
pleased to state:
(a) the State-wise details of communal
riots that took place in various parts of the
country during the last year and the current
year so far;
(b) the details of loss of life and
property in each case;
(c) the details of compensation paid to
the affected families;
(d) the details of those against whom
action has been taken/is being taken for
instigating/perpetrating the communal riots;
and
(e) whether it is a fact that in most of
these cases, minority community suffered
the most?
Personnel of para-military forces
leaving the forces
*176. SHRI S. THANGA VELU: Will
the Minister of DEFENCE be pleased to
state:
(a) whether it is a fact that nearly 30,000
personnel from para-military forces have
left the forces during the last three years;
(b) whether it is also a fact that due to
continuous posting in difficult areas, long
working hours, sleep deprivation, denial of
leave, lack of health care facilities and delay
in promotion and pay parity leading to
unbearable stress among personnel, many
personnel have left the job;
(c) if so, whether Government has
constituted any grievance redressal system
in para-military forces, especially in BSF,
ITBP etc.; and
(d) if so, the details thereof?

53
Steps taken to promote re-marriage of
widows
†*177. SHRI DARSHAN SINGH
YADAV: Will the Minister of WOMEN
AND CHILD DEVELOPMENT be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government has taken/
proposes to take any steps to promote re-
marriage of widows;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) if not, the reasons therefor?
Timely disposal of domestic violence
cases
*178. DR. T.N. SEEMA: Will the
Minister of WOMEN AND CHILD
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) the State-wise and year-wise details
of domestic violence cases registered and
disposed by courts after implementation
of the Domestic Violence Act, 2005 in the
country in the last three years;
(b) whether it is a fact that courts are
not delivering judgments within sixty days,
thereby defeating the very purpose of the
Act; and
(c) the steps taken by Government for
timely disposal of such cases?
Setting up of additional Service
Selection Boards
*179. DR. K.P. RAMALINGAM: Will
the Minister of DEFENCE be pleased to
state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Government
proposes to establish additional Service
Selection Boards;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether it is also a fact that the army
is planning intensive publicity campaigns
targetting both urban and rural areas to
attract youth to join armed forces; and
(d) if so, the details thereof?
Production capacity of cement plants
*180. SHRI BASAWARAJ PATIL: Will
the Minister of COMMERCE AND
INDUSTRY be pleased to state:
(a) the details of cement plants working
in India in both private and public sector
and their annual production capacity;
(b) the number of cement plants which
have been approved, but have not yet
started production;
(c) the details of such plants, their
owner companies and projected annual
production capacity; and
(d) the number of cement plants which
have been declared sick, public and private
sector-wise details of such plants with their
existing production level and other details?
NEW DELHI; SHUMSHER K. SHERIFF,
The 29th November, 2012 Secretary-General.
Agrahayana 8, 1934 (Saka)
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

54

55
RAJYA  SABHA
————
List of Questions for ORAL ANSWERS
to be asked at a sitting of the Rajya Sabha to be held on
Thursday, December 6, 2012/Agrahayana 15, 1934 (Saka)
————
(Ministries :  Prime Minister; Atomic Energy; Development of North Eastern
Region; External Affairs; Finance; Overseas Indian Affairs; Panchayati Raj;
Parliamentary Affairs; Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions;
Planning; Space; Steel; Tourism; Tribal Affairs; Urban
Development; Youth Affairs and Sports)
Total number of questions — 20
Decisions on the Jaitapur Atomic
Power Plant
*181. SHRI HUSAIN DALWAI: Will
the PRIME MINISTER be pleased to
state:
(a) the details of decisions taken by
Government on proposed Jaitapur Atomic
Power Plant in Maharashtra;
(b) whether any detailed programme has
been chalked out for the re-settlement of
people likely to be displaced by the
Jaitapur Plant;
(c) if so, the details thereof; and
(d) if not, the reasons therefor?
Suffering of Small Savings Agents
*182. DR. E.M. SUDARSANA
NATCHIAPPAN: Will the Minister of
FINANCE be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government is aware of the
suffering of Small Savings Agents due to the
Shyamala Gopinath Committee on the
National Small Savings Fund, not
recommending to cut the inter-departmental
commission to the Postal Department
thereby causing increase in the cost of
interest, has led to unemployment of families
depending on Agents' commission; and
(b) if so, whether Government would
use the services of Agents by attaching with
PSU banks or supplying the Electronic
Banking machines to deposit the interest
and principle directly to the Postal Banks?
Guidelines to banks for recovery of
NPA funds
*183. SHRI RAM KRIPAL YADA V:
Will the Minister of FINANCE be pleased
to state:
(a) the schemes available to persons
who have taken loans from banks which
have been declared Non-Performing Assets
(NPA), wanting to clear their liabilities to
banks;

56
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
(b) the details of those schemes and their
validity;
(c) the guidelines to banks for recovery
of NPA funds; and
(d) if so, the details thereof?
Coverage of cities under JNNURM
*184. SHRI RAJEEV CHANDRA-
SEKHAR: Will the Minister of URBAN
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) the number of cities in the State of
Karnataka which have been covered under
the Urban Infrastructure and Governance
(UIG) component of Jawaharlal  Nehru
National Urban Renewal Mission
(JNNURM);
(b) whether Government proposes to
include some more cities of the State under
UIG;
(c) if so, the details thereof and if not,
the reasons therefor; and
(d) the results achieved in the cities
which have already been covered under UIG
in the State?
Leveraging Panchayats for efficiency
*185. SHRI C.M. RAMESH: Will the
Minister of PANCHAYATI RAJ be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government contemplates
to examine the possibility of leveraging
